rules.name: Focus Breadth Electives
rules.desc:
Students in the Sustainable Coastal Systems subplan must complete at least 1 Focus Breadth Elective.
Students in the Sustainable Energy Systems, Sustainable Freshwater Systems, and Sustainable Urban Systems subplans must complete at least 2 Focus Breadth Electives.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.desc: The following choices of WIM courses are the same for all four subplans. Note that CEE100 is required for the Urban subplan, and can count as Breadth for the other subplans.

rules.name: Honors Program Overview
rules.desc:
The Environmental Systems Engineering Honors Program involves an in-depth research study in an area proposed to and agreed to by a Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering faculty adviser and completion of a thesis of high quality.
A written proposal for the research to be undertaken must be submitted and approved by the faculty advisor in the fourth quarter prior to graduation. At the time of application, the student must have an overall grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.3 for course work at Stanford; this GPA must be maintained to graduation.
The written thesis must be approved by the thesis adviser.
Students are encouraged to present their results in a seminar for faculty and students.

rules.name: Directed Writing Projects
rules.desc: The thesis is supervised by a CEE faculty adviser and must involve input from the School of Engineering’s Technical Communication Program (Huang 049) by means of ENGR 202S: Directed Writing Projects or its equivalent.

rules.name: OPTIONAL Thesis Research Support Course
rules.desc:
Up to 10 units of CEE 199H Undergraduate Honors Thesis may be taken to support the research and writing (not to duplicate ENGR 202S).
These units are beyond the normal Environmental Systems Engineering major program requirements.

rules.name: Combined GPA of 2.0 in Engineering Fundamentals and Depth courses

gpa: The Minimum Combined GPA for all Engineering Fundamentals and Depth courses is 2.0.
grading: All courses taken for the major must be taken for a letter grade if the instructor offers that option.
policies:
• Procedures and forms for requesting transfer credits and program deviations are available via links provided in the above webpage.

• With the exception of the WIM requirement, a course may only be counted toward one requirement in the major, not double-counted.
transferPolicy: Refer to the Registrar’s Transfer Credit information and our webpage for official external and transfer credit policies.
reviewNotes: Every course must be letter graded when the instructor offers a letter grade, and a course counts toward one requirement only, except that the WIM course (CEE 100 or 102W) also counts elsewhere. You pick one of the four subplans, and the audit checks its 36 units of math and science (one math sequence, not mixed, and one chemistry option), Technology in Society, Engineering Fundamentals, 40 units of depth with two Focus Breadth Electives, and the CEE 183 capstone, for 93 units in all; Urban students also take CEE 100. Your advisor checks the 2.0 GPA in fundamentals and depth courses, and honors adds a 3.3 GPA, an approved proposal and the thesis. Left: Energy's chemistry rule lists both CHEM 31A and CHEM 31E as required with no text to say otherwise, and the Electives section asks Coastal students for one breadth elective where the subplan asks for two; the subplan's two is used.
